title: How To Find Mysidia In Final Fantasy: Resonance
description: Final Fantasy: Resonance grants you an airship around halfway through its main story, giving you the ability to fly nearly anywhere you'd like across the world map. However, not too long after finally taking to the skies, you'll need to find the hidden city of Mysidia. Finding Mysidia can prove frustrating if you're not quite sure what area to be looking in. Lucky for you, in this guide, we'll fill you in on exactly where to find Mysidia in Final Fantasy: Resonance. Where to find Mysidia in Final Fantasy: Resonance When you start Chapter 5 of Final Fantasy: Resonance, you'll need to discover the hidden city of Mysidia. To do so, you'll need to use a newly equipped radar system that has been attached to your airship. When you're flying around the world map, you can press the right trigger to send out a ping, and Lid will comment whether or not it's picking up any traces of Mysidia. You can fly around the map pinging randomly until Lid starts noticing traces, then follow her directions, but that can prove slightly frustrating. If you'd rather skip the search, we'll simply tell you how to find Mysidia. Pass between these landmasses and go further south to find Mysidia. To find Mysidia, head to the very southern portion of the map. Note the large mass of the Kingdom of Pharm (left) and two small islands seen in the photo above. Pass between the landmasses and head slightly further south, then use your ping to unveil Mysidia. Later in the game, this pinging radar system comes into play again to aid you in finding treasure across the world map. As with finding Mysidia, you'll just need to fly around pinging until Lid picks up on something, then follow her guidance to help you round up some fresh loot. Happy hunting! You'll have an opportunity to use the radar again later in the game. Final Fantasy: Resonance is available now on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC. For more on this HD-2D JRPG, you can check out how long it takes to beat Final…

title: Final Fantasy Resonance’s First Boss Will Give You Hell Unless You Grab These Key Items
description: You'll come up against a handful of tutorial bosses during Chapter 1 of Final Fantasy: Resonance 's lengthy adventure. However, none will pose nearly the challenge of its first esper boss, Siren, whom you'll find awaiting you at the top of her spiral tower. This tough opponent can hit hard and cast Charm on your party, which certainly poses a problem if you're not prepared to deal with it. But don't worry, as we've got some tips for dealing with Siren below. How to beat Siren in Final Fantasy: Resonance When Siren reaches around half health, she'll begin using an attack called Allure, which will immediately cast Charm on your entire party. Charm causes your characters to attack one another, which can cause damage to add up quickly. If you aren't prepared to combat Charm casts--on Normal or Expert difficulty especially--there's a reasonable chance Siren will get the best of your party. Monk's Prayer Beads are the way to go for Charm nullification. Luckily, there are three ways you can prepare to nullify this annoying effect ahead of time--though there's definitely one that stands above the rest, which we'll tell you about at the end of this list. Monk's Prayer Beads - This accessory nullifies Charm on whoever is wearing it. You can purchase two of these from the armor merchant in Granport Harbor for 1,500 gil each, or you can obtain them naturally. One can be easily found in a chest on your way up the tower to the boss, while another can be obtained by completing the very straightforward Secrets Unearthed sidequest from Chloe in Felicitas. Equipping Leah - You can grant one character Charm immunity by simply having Leah equipped to them. Her "Nullify Charm" passive assures at least one party member is safe, and we'd recommend that be Fina if necessary. Read on for why that is. Esuna or Pray - Esuna is a spell that can cure any ailment, and Pray is an ability that does the same thing. Since Siren can occasionally cast Silence on a character, Pray becomes unusable.…

title: How Long Is Final Fantasy: Resonance – Chapter List And Total Hours
description: Final Fantasy: Resonance is the first HD-2D entry in Square Enix's long-running role-playing franchise, offering players a way to experience something both classic and new at the same time. With a story and gameplay mechanics that find a unique way to blend classic characters with an all-new cast, this one's no doubt a great spot for new players and returning fans to jump in. If you're wondering how long it takes to see this HD-2D journey through, though, we've got you covered. Here's how long it takes to beat Final Fantasy: Resonance. In This Article How long it takes to beat Final Fantasy: Resonance Final Fantasy: Resonance chapter list How long it takes to beat Final Fantasy: Resonance An average playthrough of Final Fantasy: Resonance takes around 30-40 hours. This includes seeing the core story through while doing a handful of side quests, plus some optional objectives like finding Visions, espers, and more. This makes it a fairly hefty JRPG experience right out of the gate, but completionists will find that their playtime can be extended by nearly double if going for 100%. Especially for those seeking to obtain every trophy or achievement, Final Fantasy: Resonance can easily take 70+ hours to see and do everything it has to offer. Final Fantasy: Resonance is best when you play it your way. Of course, those who want to mainline the story, or who opt to play on Casual difficulty, may reach the game's conclusion more quickly. Meanwhile, choosing the hardest difficulty may add enough challenge that you could see your playtime exceed 80 hours. How you decide to experience Final Fantasy: Resonance is entirely up to you, so play it on the difficulty that feels right. And there's no need to feel obligated to see and do everything, as you can mostly just engage with the parts that you enjoy along the way to seeing how the game's epic story concludes. Final Fantasy: Resonance chapter list Final Fantasy: Resonance is split into eight chapters, which play out linearly.…

title: In Final Fantasy: Resonance, Take This Early Detour To Unlock Cloud Strife
description: Few characters in the Final Fantasy series are as recognizable and universally adored as Cloud Strife from Final Fantasy VII. So, it makes sense that Final Fantasy: Resonance would include the snarky mercenary in its cast of Visions, which function as equippable characters that aid your party. If you're looking to get your hands on Cloud as soon as possible, you'll be happy to hear that this popular spiky-haired fellow can be added to your party within the first few hours of the game. Here's how to get Cloud in Final Fantasy: Resonance. How to get Cloud Strife in Final Fantasy: Resonance As with all Visions in Final Fantasy: Resonance, obtaining Cloud requires you to visit his respective sanctum in the overworld. Luckily, for fans of this beloved hero, the Sanctum of Cloud becomes available quite early in the adventure during Chapter 1. However, it requires a bit of a detour, which means you could potentially miss it if you're not thoroughly exploring. After the initial events at the Earth Shrine play out, you'll soon find yourself journeying to the desert in the west. It's in this area of the overworld that you'll find the Sanctum of Cloud, but you'll want to wrap up your brief visit to the Village of Kol first. You won't be able to reach the sanctum from this side of the desert. Instead, wait until you've made your way all the way to the west of this portion of the continent to reach Grandport Harbor. You'll be spending quite a bit of time there for the main story, but for now, we'll just use it as a starting point for our journey to the Sanctum of Cloud. Head across this bridge to reach the portion of the desert housing the Sanctum of Cloud. From Grandport Harbor, head north, then take the bridge slightly to the east. Immediately after crossing over the sand waterfall on the other side, head all the way north. Pass the cave here and wrap around south to spot the Sanctum of Cloud. Here's where to find the Sanctum of Cloud. Refer to the map above for the exact…

title: Your Favorite Video Games Will Always Be Influenced By Manga
description: In the heart of Brooklyn, there is now a devastatingly gorgeous manga panel from Jiro Taniguchi's Ice Age: Chronicle of the Earth hung on a gallery wall. I can't tell you what it says--I fear my scant familiarity with Japanese doesn't extend to literacy in kanji--but I can tell you what it portrays: a cityscape consumed by nature. A lush tangle of vines and trees reclaiming the Earth from its disastrous, mettlesome inheritors. While I doubt this panel and manga are the first time this kind of image has cropped up, it certainly feels like a progenitor to many similar visuals across the years. Your mind might jump to I Am Legend, the Will Smith-led feature film about a post-apocalyptic New York City, for example. My mind jumped straight to Nier Automata's city that's been lost to time, as well as The Last of Us' many dilapidated small towns and US metropolises. Though I went into the Brooklyn Museum's new Art of Manga exhibit already curious about what connections the form might have to games, it became quickly apparent that manga has always been in conversation with other mediums, influencing everything from anime to gaming. The Brooklyn Museum, located right near Prospect Park in New York City, is currently home to the Art of Manga exhibit. Curated by Nicole Coolidge Rousmaniere--whose love of manga stems from early exposure to French graphic novels and reading Astro Boy at a seminal age--the gallery features a beautiful selection of Taniguchi’s work, as well as select other notable mangaka (manga artists and authors) of outsized influence. This includes Rumiko Takahashi, best known for her work on Ranma ½ and Inuyasha, Eiichiro Oda, the renowned creator of One Piece, and Hirohiko Araki, whose gorgeously styled illustrations from Jojo’s Bizarre Adventure are among the exhibits crown jewels. In total, the exhibit draws from the work of 10 mangaka, evenly split between male and female authors of varying popularity and prefectures of Japan, and explores different…

title: Max Miller’s Tasting History Is Coming To Your Tabletop With A New Board Game
description: Behind his cheerful delivery and presentation, it turns out that Max Miller, known for turning historical recipes into entertaining yet educational YouTube lessons with his show Tasting History, is also quite serious about board games. Now, game designer Michael Shinall (Marvel Zombies, DCeased, and others) and publisher Salt Games are working with Max to bring him from his kitchen straight to your tabletop with a brand-new worker-placement game based on his popular series, which launched on Kickstarter this week. Recently, we had the chance to sit down with both Max and Michael to hear about how this new adaptation will play, a bit about how it all came to be, and why, whether you are coming at this as a fan of Tasting History or board games, there will be something on this plate you may like. In Tasting History: The Board Game, each player works to collect ingredients from various locations on the board, which they use to cook and prepare delicious, historically accurate recipes. They host parties and progress through ages, watching the offerings grow with the passing of time. Featured in the base box will be three different historical periods, including ancient Rome, medieval Europe, and the American Frontier, each highlighting 25 unique recipes from the period and various historical events. Tasting History: The Board Game The game itself is split into five rounds, with 1-5 players taking turns placing their four chefs at the various spots on the era’s board, and is completed in only about 60-90 minutes. Each of the six main locations allows players to gather ingredients required to complete their recipes and provide other benefits. Additionally, players may collect special Insight cards, which Michael elaborated on: “[Insight Cards] are different little bonuses that let you cheat in some way or gain an advantage when the conditions are met. These can range from giving you free ingredients to giving you extra bonus victory points to letting you do things when…

title: The Halo We Grew Up With Is Never Coming Back
description: It has been less than two years since Xbox announced that longtime series developer 343 Industries would be rebranding to Halo Studios. This was envisioned as a new dawn for the beloved shooter franchise, as Xbox seemed to leave the Reclaimer Trilogy behind as it sought to tighten Master Chief’s focus to enable a more faithful and satisfying future. As someone who always held out hope for Halo regardless of how dire things seemed, I was legitimately convinced that this reformed studio was destined for bigger and brighter things. I became even more reassured following the July release of Campaign Evolved, a confident remake that despite polarising reception amongst hardcore audiences, did its job of pulling a fading icon back into the limelight. If the next steps were carefully made, we could have been living in a reality where Halo took over the world again. But with Microsoft obliterating Halo Studios with 268 layoffs and putting the series’ future under the Activision umbrella, my fading flame has finally flickered out. Whatever form it takes in the coming years with a new team and a refreshed creative vision, I simply cannot bring myself to care anymore. The Halo I grew up with is gone, and the cheering I have done from the sidelines for all these years has been for nothing. I wish this weren’t the case, because there were so many moments over the years that oozed potential. Halo 4 dove into more compelling lore than Bungie ever did, while it was amazing to watch 343 Industries flesh Master Chief out into more than a stoic naval officer. He is far more complex: a child soldier bred for warfare and robbed of personal agency so much that the only meaningful relationship he has is with an artificial intelligence destined to eventually leave him behind. title: Star Wars Battlefront 3 Reportedly In Development By EA’s Top Shooter Studios
description: Included in the shocking news of EA's restructuring, which includes layoffs and the closure of BioWare, is a mention from the publisher that Apex Legends studio Respawn Entertainment and Battlefield maker DICE are collaborating on a project. According to a report, that project is a long-awaited sequel set in a galaxy far, far away. Per Variety, which cites "multiple sources," the DICE and Respawn project is Star Wars Battlefront 3. While EA itself did not confirm this, the company's memo about the restructuring says that the studios' title will contribute to EA's goal of delivering a "shooter portfolio that unlocks growth." EA specifically states that learnings from Battlefield 6's launch and live service will further that goal, while also announcing that Apex Legends will be expanded with new "gameplay modes" and "other new experiences." As for the purported existence of Star Wars Battlefront 3, the timing coincides with a recent rumor that Lucasfilm Games was seeking a development partner for a new Battlefront, and that DICE and Sony-owned studio Bungie were among the studios being considered. DICE had made two Star Wars Battlefront games for EA, which were released in 2015 and 2017. Battlefront 2 attracted criticism over loot boxes (remember when that was the hot controversy of the day?), but the game still proved to be massively popular. Last year, Battlefront 2 suddenly had a resurgence in players, with many hoping that it would ignite talks of a third Battlefront. Outside of Battlefront and shooters, the Star Wars franchise has gained two new popular entries this year alone, with strategy game Star Wars Zero Company (which Respawn co-developed) and racing title Star Wars: Galactic Racer enjoying critical success.

title: Xbox Cloud Gaming Hourly Prices Revealed For Non-Game Pass Members
description: Microsoft has revealed how much it will charge people for using the Xbox Cloud Gaming service without a Game Pass membership. Right now, this is available only to Xbox Insiders, but that's a free program that anyone can join. Also notable is that the prices below are described as "introductory launch pricing," and that wording suggests the prices may change in the future. Microsoft is calling these "cloud playtime packs." Cloud playtime packs pricing: 10 hours for $4 25 hours for $8 50 hours for $12 Anyone who buys these cloud playtime packs will get access to cloud gaming without ads and with perks like shorter wait times and higher-quality streaming. These packs will be available to more people starting in November. A version of Xbox cloud gaming with ads is also available to Xbox Insiders without a Game Pass membership. As for those who do have a Game Pass membership, changes are coming to cloud gaming in November. Microsoft will put limits on how many hours per month people can use the service, and then allow people to pay more to unlock more time. Below is a breakdown of how many hours you’ll get included with the tier of Game Pass you’re subscribed to: Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours Game Pass Premium: 10 hours Game Pass Essential: 5 hours Microsoft said it understands this is a “meaningful change,” especially for those who use the cloud regularly for gaming. However, the company said it estimates that these changes will impact about 4% of Game Pass subscribers, though the company did not share any specifics on how it arrived at that projection. In other Game Pass news, it was recently reported that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is considering a massive shakeup to the service to allow people to build their own Game Pass and choose which features they do and do not want.

title: Don’t Worry, You’re Not The Only One Dying Too Much In Modern Warfare 4’s Campaign
description: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 releases this week, and the campaign and DMZ are currently in early access. Infinity Ward delivers an epic series conclusion for its Modern Warfare reboot, but if you're finding some missions tough on a normal difficulty setting, don't worry–you're not alone. Modern Warfare 4 features 16 missions in total, and these offer a wide variety of staple Call of Duty missions, such as stealth ops, cinematic chase sequences, and a slow-motion breach-and-clear scenario. There are also a couple of intense melee-style boss fights, where your life depends on well-timed parrying. As a longtime Call of Duty player who typically plays through all the campaigns on both normal and veteran difficulties, Modern Warfare 4's normal difficulty feels tougher than what we've experienced in the last few years. This takes me back to Infinity Ward's most recent game, Modern Warfare 2, when the NPCs also felt like much more formidable opponents. It was easy to underestimate the AI's ability to overwhelm you, and they always seemed just smart enough to sniff you out during stealth missions. The NPCs aren't necessarily more intelligent in Modern Warfare 4, but they do feel like they are buffed up and shooting straighter this year, so trying to rush through their defenses can be unwise. I was humbled more than a few times when trying to clear out an area with a large presence of enemy soldiers, and I had to repeat one of the boss fights more than I'd like to admit. I've heard this same complaint from others playing Modern Warfare 4's campaign, so surely this isn't an age or skill issue, but Infinity Ward delivering another challenging campaign. Overall, Modern Warfare 4 on normal difficulty isn't too painful and definitely a manageable setting to play on, but it has forced me to play slower and show more patience. I'll still give the campaign a try on the veteran setting, but that's the highest challenge I'm aiming for. For those eager for an ultimate test of skill,…

title: EA Cancels New Mass Effect, Pauses New Sims Game, And All The Other Big EA News That Just Happened
description: When EA was acquired by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, many expected major changes at the gaming company, including layoffs and game cancellations, among other shakeups. Now, those have begun, with EA on October 21 confirming a series of significant changes impacting the people and teams that worked on many storied franchises. EA also teased some of what's to come in the future, including a joint project between Respawn and DICE. Here's a rundown of all the big EA news today. Layoffs EA said in a statement that it made the "difficult" choice to lay off staff, and Bloomberg reported that the cuts will impact about 400 people. Affected staffers will be treated with "care and respect," EA said, and some impacted employees may have a chance to get a different job within EA. Alongside the BioWare closure noted below, staff at Ripple Effect (Battlefield), Maxis (The Sims), and Full Circle (Skate) have been impacted, as noted by Vertical Slice. BioWare closes and new Mass Effect axed BioWare, the esteemed Canadian developer founded 30+ years ago, is shutting down. The studio employed fewer than 100 people, Bloomberg reported, and the team was working on the next Mass Effect. That game is now canceled. "BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly," EA said. Developers at BioWare had feared their jobs were at risk after PIF announced that it would buy EA. BioWare is known, in part, for making pro-diversity games featuring inclusive storytelling and characters. Longtime BioWare writer Patrick Weekes, who was laid off in 2025, speculated that EA’s new owners, including the PIF, might want to avoid “gay stuff” and politics that the PIF’s leadership does not agree with. There has been an outpouring of support and thoughtful messages about BioWare in the wake of the news, from fans and industry professionals alike. CD Projekt's Michal Nowakowski said his company first got to know BioWare when the…

title: Rayman Legends Retold’s New Baguette Costumes Are A Tip Of The Beret To Expedition 33
description: Rayman Legends Retold is almost here, and as you'd expect from this remake, it's a pretty noticeable graphical glow-up of Rayman Legends and it includes a very French outfit for you to dress the phantom-limbed hero and his partner Barbara up in. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 fans, this is where you do the Leonardo DiCaprio pointing meme. Even though Ubisoft doesn't mention Sandfall Interactive or Expedition 33 by name, it did confirm that the new baguette outfits are "a playful nod to a fellow game" created in Montpellier. "Conceived as a tribute from one French studio to another, these costumes celebrate the creativity, passion, and unmistakably French touch that continue to make the country's video game industry shine on the global stage," Ubisoft said in a press release. Sandfall Interactive is also headquartered in Montpellier. The friendly homage is no doubt a tribute to Sandfall Interactive and its award-winning debut game, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. The Expedition 33 outfit features a white shirt with black pinstripes, black pants with black suspenders, a red beret, and a baguette kept inside a red-and-white plaid cloth, making it as Gallic as Groundskeeper Willie's introduction to the beautiful French language. Unlocking the outfit for each character in the hit RPG isn't easy, as players must defeat secret mime mini-bosses around the map. The look isn't unique to either game, as the ensemble draws on 19th-century naval uniforms, Basque headwear, and "Onion Johnny" door-to-door traders. Over time, those fashion elements became synonymous with France, becoming a symbol of French elegance and casual style that artists like Pablo Picasso and fashion icon Jean Paul Gaultier adopted. You've probably also spotted people wearing these costumes at conventions, as Expedition 33's baguette outfits make for an easy, low-cost, and comfortable cosplay. Ubisoft says the baguette costumes will be available to all players at launch, when the game launches for PC, PS5, Xbox…

title: Another Day, Another Pokemon Card Heist Worth Nearly $1 Million
description: I guess someone's gotta collect 'em all, and it appears that thieves are doing just that, as yet another high-stakes burglary in Southern California has resulted in just about $1 million worth of Pokemon cards being stolen from a FedEx truck. According to a report by The New York Times' sports journalism department, The Athletic (via ABC News ), a FedEx truck parked near the authenticating and grading business known as the Professional Sports Authenticator in Santa Ana, California, was robbed on October 13. The Santa Ana Police Department said in a statement to ABC News that hundreds of cards were stolen, with the robbery estimated at a value of $963,000. "The pallets contained various trading cards, including, but not limited to, sports cards and Pokemon cards," the Santa Ana Police Department said in a statement. "However, the exact value of the stolen items has not yet been determined." According to the Santa Ana Police Department, the thieves broke into the FedEx truck, stole two full pallets of cards, and tore through a third pallet for even more packaged goodies--all of which belonged to collectors from across the country who submitted their cards to the Professional Sports Authenticator to be authenticated and graded for collecting or reselling purposes. Collectors, the parent company of the Professional Sports Authenticator, told ABC News that in the wake of the theft, it has deactivated the certificates for the missing cards and notified its other businesses in its marketplace to "be on the lookout" for the cards in case they turn up. "We are aware of a theft involving a third-party shipping vehicle carrying PSA-graded items," the company said. "We are working closely with law enforcement and the carrier as the investigation continues. Our customer service team has contacted affected customers directly and is arranging compensation based on fair market value. We understand the impact this has on collectors involved, many of whom see these cards as far more…

title: EA Shuts Down Dragon Age, Mass Effect Studio BioWare
description: Publisher Electronic Arts is planning to shut down legendary RPG studio BioWare, laying off about 50 employees at the studio alongside 350 more elsewhere. In a new Bloomberg report, a person familiar with the matter said a total of 3% of EA's overall company has been affected by this latest round of layoffs. BioWare posted a statement to X, confirming that it's shutting down and thanking everyone for their support over the studio's lifetime. It's quite a sad day. "There is nothing easy about writing these words," BioWare said. "Our focus right now is on our incredibly talented team who put their hearts into these games, and supporting one another through this transition. What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember. These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with the characters, and made these worlds your own." In a staff letter sent out on Wednesday that has now been shared by the company, EA chief operating officer David Tinson and chief studios officer Cam Weber explained that the company took a "hard look" at its business over the last several months. This resulted in some projects getting canceled, including the next Mass Effect game-- which was in early development at BioWare --as well as a planned game in The Sims franchise codenamed Project Lotus. Instead, the resources allocated to that title will be diverted to something else currently codenamed Project Evergreen. Many of EA's currently released franchises will continue as expected. Full Circle will keep working on Skate, but EA said the team there would be downsized. Meanwhile, its myriad sports games, Apex Legends, Battlefield, the next Star Wars Jedi game, and a new game based on Iron Man will continue to be invested in. "Across our portfolio, we're making deliberate choices to align talent and investments where we see the greatest opportunities for players and long-term growth," Tinson and Weber wrote in the letter.…

title: Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 update adds two new quests, handgun dual wielding and the ability to pimp your mantis blades
description: A beefy new Cyberpunk 2077 update arrives tomorrow, October 22nd, fresh on the heels of the second series of the Cyberpunk Edgerunners anime which dropped earlier this week. It's dubbed update 2.5 and delivers an Edgerunners 2-themed quest alongside a heap of other additions. Read more

title: CD Projekt Red details new Cyberpunk 2077 update - adding dual-wielding, cross-platform mods, Edgerunners story quests, and more
description: CD Projekt Red has detailed the substantial update coming to Cyberpunk 2077, revealing a new dual-wielding skill for pistols and revolvers, cyberware customisation, cross-platform mod support, and a brand-new Edgerunners-related story quest featuring voice actors from the Netflix anime show.
